Something very interesting about this paper.

Frontier LLMs treat math proofs very differently to physics proofs.

If you ask a frontier LLM to analyse the repo they will dismiss it as empirical physics

If you ask it to treat it like an axiom under the axiomatic method as pure maths or reconstruct the tree themselves as pure math they love it

I think this has to do with the move from Hilbert era axiomatic method and seeing where the math led to to Einstein and beyond getting more and more constructive

If you look at back at the time of Hilbert and co there are actually some interesting thigns that blocked the axiomatic approach as I'll cover in future releases

For Hilbert on GR it was getting distracted by Mies electrodynamics even though the math didn't support it

In general as a preview what I found following the math is that the biggest blockers were - assuming Poincare is just a limit (despite Whitehead's lemma) and fine for QM etc, assuming gravity is geometry and also assuming the metric is the base (!)

Poke around and if using AI do ask it to check its own work and reread the paper if it gets stuck, it will show some very interesting things.

Memory name buybacks + pricing projections:  

- $SKHY doubled its daily buybacks from ~$290M -> $581M, after Korea relaxed its buyback rules, explicitly citing "undervaluation"
- $MU Dec 9, 2026 marks the end of the first 2 under initial CHIPS act agreements (where there was restrictions on buybacks). 

Micron stated it expects to return 100% of excess cash to shareholders, and that they'll increase returns past Dec 9th. 

On the supply/pricing side per Trendforce: 

- Conventional DRAM contract price increases are expected to narrow throughout 2027, with prices potentially leveling off in the H2 2027 before declining in 2028

Under the assumptions that: 
--- Consumer electronics manufacturers are facing mounting sales pressure
--- Chinese CSPs scaling back DRAM demand in early 4Q26 (but absorbed by US CSPs)
--- markets expect a cautious policy stance toward domestic DC development
--- $NVDA scales back its financing support for neocloud providers.

They forecast conventional DRAM to increase 10%-15% Q4 2026, with further increases up 3%-8% Q1 2027. 

In another bear case they give:
--- server OEMs will further scale back procurement following downward revisions to demand
--- widespread inventory reductions across the supply chain
--- downside risks include reduced investment and potential consolidation among neocloud providers

"overall server shipment growth could begin decelerating as early as 2027, causing conventional DRAM contract prices to reverse course and begin declining in 4Q27, with price declines widening in 2028."

___

$MU CEO said earlier: "we expect memory and storage supply demand conditions to be much tighter in 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026"...

But I think everyone is starting to price in a 2028 demand/pricing destruction already (which hasn't happened). Also I do think a lot of new price floor LTAs should change how we look at memory name durability.

As long as durability and pricing remains elevated for longer periods of time, which $SKHY likely has more information to, I'd agree with them shares look increasingly undervalued.

Hyperliquid's biggest winners could fund the apps that come next.

New apps need early users and liquidity before anyone else will take a chance on them. On Ethereum and Solana, much of that came from people who had already made money on those chains. 

Hyperliquid's traders and HYPE holders are in that position now.

So far most of what they've put onchain has gone into staking and lending. That is partly because HyperEVM has been difficult to build on and launched without much spending on integrations or marketing.

On Kinetiq's Elysium, apps have far more room and builders get a quarter of every transaction fee. That share would come to about $19 million a year if Elysium earned as much in fees as Base did in 2025. 

That gives teams a strong reason to pick Elysium when choosing where to build.

Canadian founders don't need more announcements about handouts, they need fewer forms and fewer obstacles.

I really don't this is complicated.
